failures.root_cause: generate_learned_rules() in scripts/lib/outcome-feedback.sh computes 'confidence' via a bc pipeline whose result (or lack of bc) can yield an empty/invalid value passed to jq's --arg confidence + tonumber, causing that jq invocation to fail after '> "$tmp_file"' already truncated the temp file; the truncated/empty file then gets read on a later call, producing the 'Expected JSON value (while parsing '')' error and zero learned rules.
failures.fix: Validate the bc/confidence output before passing to jq (e.g. `[[ "$confidence" =~ ^[0-9.]+$ ]] || confidence=0.6`), write via a fresh mktemp per iteration, and only mv the tmp file into place when jq succeeds and produced non-empty valid JSON.
